  6. Enter your article in the Content editor
  7. Click Save
  8. Result: The article is created for the audience you selected. If Send notification is set to Yes, MOS sends a notification to that audience.

Captured 25 October 2026.

Fields:

  • Title (required): The article headline
  • Audience (required): Who receives this article. Choose All Users for everyone or select a specific subgroup
  • Send notification (required): Whether to email the article to your audience
  • Content (required): The full article text

Tips:

  • Keep titles clear and descriptive
  • Target specific subgroups when the news only affects certain members
  • Send email notifications for important announcements

docs.title: Use AI Rewrite for Article Content
docs.text:
When the AI features add-on is active and your role has AI Rewrite access, the Content editor shows a purple AI Rewrite button.

  1. Write the article draft.
  2. Select a passage to rewrite only that passage, or leave the text unselected to rewrite the whole article.
  3. Click AI Rewrite.
  4. Review the replacement text for accuracy, tone, dates, and audience details.
  5. Make any corrections, then click Save when the article is ready.

AI Rewrite does not publish or email the article by itself. See AI Features for access settings and troubleshooting.

docs.title: How to Edit an Article
docs.text:
1. Navigate to Admin then News Management
  2. Find the article you want to edit
  3. Click Edit
  4. Update the title, audience, or content
  5. Click Save
  6. Result: The article is updated immediately

docs.title: How to Delete an Article
docs.text:
1. Navigate to Admin then News Management
  2. Find the article you want to delete
  3. Click Delete
  4. Confirm the deletion when prompted
  5. Result: The article is permanently removed from the news feed

docs.title: Email-to-News (Optional Feature)
docs.text:
Your group may have Email-to-News enabled, which allows you to create news articles by sending an email to a designated mailbox.

Captured 25 October 2026.

docs.title: How to Use Email-to-News
docs.text:
1. On the News Management page, find the Email-to-News section (if enabled for your group)
  2. Note the mailbox address provided (e.g., mos-news@matchofficialsystem.com)
  3. Send an email to that address with:
    • Subject: The article title
    • Body: The article content
    • Attachments: Any files to include with the article
  4. Result: The article is automatically created and sent to all members in your group

Tips:

  • Keep subjects concise and descriptive
  • Format your email body clearly (line breaks will be preserved)
  • Attachments should be reasonable file sizes
  • Articles created via email follow the same targeting as manual articles (applies to entire group)

Note

The sender's email address must match someone with Communications or Owner role in the group. If the email doesn't match, the message will be rejected.

docs.title: No articles appear on the News page
docs.text:
Symptoms: The News page shows no articles

How to Fix:

  1. Check that you are logged in to your account
  2. Verify you have membership in at least one group or association
  3. Check with your administrator to confirm articles have been published
  4. Try refreshing the page

Common Causes:

  • No articles have been published for your association or subgroups
  • Your membership may not include access to published news

docs.title: Articles I created don't appear
docs.text:
Symptoms: News article created but not visible to members

How to Fix:

  1. Verify the audience is set correctly:
    • Check if you selected All Users or a subgroup
    • Only members of the selected audience can see the article
  2. Check that the article was saved successfully (look for confirmation message)
  3. Try refreshing the news page
  4. Verify members are actually part of the audience group

Common Causes:

  • Article is targeted to wrong audience
  • Members are not subscribed to the audience subgroup
  • Article was not saved successfully

docs.title: Attachments don't download
docs.text:
Symptoms: Clicking an attachment doesn't open or download the file

How to Fix:

  1. Refresh the page and try again
  2. Check your internet connection
  3. Verify you are logged in
  4. Try a different file if multiple attachments exist
  5. Contact your administrator if the problem continues

Common Causes:

  • The file may have been removed
  • Temporary network issue
  • File may be too large

docs.title: Email notification not received
docs.text:
Symptoms: Members didn't receive email after publishing article

How to Fix:

  1. Check that Send notification was set to Yes when creating the article
  2. Verify members have email addresses in their profiles
  3. Check their email spam or junk folder
  4. Ask members to check their email preferences (unsubscribe setting)

Common Causes:

  • Notification was set to No instead of Yes
  • Members have opted out of email notifications
  • Email was filtered as spam

docs.title: Related Pages
docs.text:
• AI Features: Rewrite news article content
  • News: View news articles as a regular user
  • User Management: Manage member access and groups

docs.title: Admin: Subgroup Membership
docs.text:
Owner access required

Only users with Owner access can manage subgroup membership.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This guide explains how to add members to subgroups and how subgroup access affects visibility, notifications and reviews.

Note

Subgroups are available when they are enabled for your organisation.

How to Access

From the main menu select Admin then Membership and Roles

Before You Start

Make sure you understand the access levels and roles, and how they apply at group and subgroup level.

  • User Standard member with personal workspace access
  • Viewer Can create assessments on other users and view subgroup folders
  • Reviewer Can review diary and plan entries, run reports, and view subgroup folders
  • Trainer Can manage exams (group-level only)
  • Communications Can manage news articles (group-level only)
  • Files Manager Can upload, delete, and organise files and folders
  • Appointer Can manage appointments and availability
  • Selector Can access depth charting
  • Owner Full administrative control (group-level only)

docs.title: Membership and Permissions
docs.text:
Subgroups give you a way to narrow visibility and actions inside a group. People can have one level in the group and a different level in one or more subgroups.

  • Group level access applies across the whole group
  • Subgroup level access only applies within that subgroup
  • Owner is only available at group level (subgroups cannot have Owners)

docs.title: How to Manage Membership
docs.text:
Captured 25 October 2026.

Captured 25 October 2026.

When adding someone to a subgroup, search for their name, select the member, then choose the access level and any roles that apply. The available subgroup roles are shown in the form.

  1. Go to Admin > Membership and Roles
  2. Find the group and the subgroup you want to manage
  3. Expand the subgroup row
  4. Click Add Member on that subgroup's row
  5. Search for a member, select them, choose the available access level and roles, then click Add Member
  6. Result: The member is added to that subgroup with the selected access

docs.title: Edit an existing member's roles
docs.text:
1. Expand the subgroup
  2. Click Edit permission on the member's row
  3. Select or clear the roles they need
  4. Click Save Changes
  5. Result: MOS confirms the permissions update and refreshes the membership list

Captured 25 October 2026.

Tip

  • Use the role filter to quickly show members by role
  • You can remove a member using Remove on their row
  • Subgroup membership has its own Add Member control. The available roles differ from group-level roles.

docs.title: What happens with Notifications and Reviews
docs.text:
• Notifications: When a subgroup is selected, notifications go to group Owners and Reviewers, plus the subgroup’s Reviewers. If no subgroup is selected, only the group Owners and Reviewers are notified.
  • Reviews: Group-level Reviewers can review items across the whole group. Subgroup Reviewers can only review items for members of the same subgroup(s).

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: The diagrams below show which people can see, get notified, or review. Shapes inside the group show subgroup membership.

docs.title: Example 1: Group-level reviewer sees everything in the group
docs.text:
Hold "Alt" / "Option" to enable pan & zoom 
flowchart LR
  subgraph Group
    Trevor["Trevor Lee (User)"]
    Jane["Jane Smith (Viewer)"]
    Alice["Alice Brown (Reviewer)"]
    Mike["Mike Chan (Reviewer)"]
    Sarah["Sarah Kim (Reviewer)"]
    David["David Ng (Reviewer)"]
    subgraph Subgroup One
      Emma[Emma Park]
      Liam[Liam Reed]
    end
    subgraph Subgroup Two
      Noah[Noah Young]
      Ava[Ava Cole]
    end
    John["John Doe (Group Reviewer)"]
    John --> Trevor & Jane & Alice & Mike & Sarah & David & Emma & Liam & Noah & Ava
  end

Result: The group-level Reviewer can review for anyone in the group, including all subgroups.

docs.title: Example 2: Subgroup reviewer only sees their subgroup
docs.text:
Hold "Alt" / "Option" to enable pan & zoom 
flowchart TD
  subgraph Group
    Trevor["Trevor Lee (User)"]
    Jane["Jane Smith (Viewer)"]
    Alice["Alice Brown (Reviewer)"]
    Mike["Mike Chan (Reviewer)"]
    Sarah["Sarah Kim (Reviewer)"]
    David["David Ng (Reviewer)"]
    subgraph Subgroup One
      Emma[Emma Park]
      Liam[Liam Reed]
      Tom["Tom Walker (Reviewer - Subgroup One)"]
    end
    subgraph Subgroup Two
      Noah[Noah Young]
      Ava[Ava Cole]
    end
    Tom --> Emma & Liam
  end

Result: The subgroup Reviewer can review for members of Subgroup One only.

docs.title: Example 3: Assigning a reviewer from the wrong subgroup
docs.text:
Hold "Alt" / "Option" to enable pan & zoom 
flowchart LR
  subgraph Group
    subgraph Subgroup One
      John["John Doe (Assigned)"]
    end
    subgraph Subgroup Two
      Trevor["Trevor Lee (Reviewer)"]
    end
  end

Result: The Reviewer in Subgroup Two cannot be assigned to review for a member in Subgroup One. They do not appear as an available reviewer.

docs.title: Example 4: Reviewer in multiple subgroups
docs.text:
Hold "Alt" / "Option" to enable pan & zoom 
flowchart LR
  subgraph Group
    subgraph Subgroup One
      Emma[Emma Park]
    end
    subgraph Subgroup Two
      Noah[Noah Young]
    end
    Jane["Jane Smith (Reviewer - Subgroup One & Two)"]
    Jane --> Emma & Noah
  end

Result: The Reviewer can review for members in both subgroups they belong to.

docs.title: Example 5: Notifications when a subgroup is selected
docs.text:
Hold "Alt" / "Option" to enable pan & zoom 
flowchart LR
  subgraph Group
    Bob[Bob Owner]
    John["John Doe (Group Reviewer)"]
    subgraph Subgroup One
      Trevor["Trevor Lee (Subgroup Reviewer)"]
    end
  end

Result: If an entry is created for Subgroup One, notifications go to the group’s Owners and Reviewers and to Subgroup One’s Reviewers.

docs.title: Example 6: Notifications when no subgroup is selected
docs.text:
Hold "Alt" / "Option" to enable pan & zoom 
flowchart LR
  subgraph Group
    Bob[Bob Owner]
    John["John Doe (Group Reviewer)"]
    subgraph Subgroup One
      Trevor["Trevor Lee (Subgroup Reviewer)"]
    end
  end

Result: If no subgroup is selected, notifications go to the group’s Owners and Reviewers only. Subgroup Reviewers are not notified.

docs.title: Field Details and Messages
docs.text:
Required vs optional

  • Group level: User, Viewer, Reviewer, Trainer, Communications, Files Manager, Owner are available
  • Subgroup level: User, Viewer, Reviewer, Files Manager, Appointer and Selector are available (Trainer, Communications and Owner are group-level only)

Common messages

  • "Member added." after saving a new member
  • "Permissions updated." after changing a level
  • "Member removed." after removing a member
  • "No groups found." if the search returns no results

Validation tips

  • Use at least 2 characters when searching
  • To add someone to a subgroup, they do not need to be in the parent group first (adding at subgroup level is allowed)

docs.title: Related Pages
docs.text:
• Membership and Roles: Manage group and subgroup membership
  • Levels of Access: Detailed explanation of each role
  • Groups and Associations: Overview of how groups and subgroups are structured
  • Groups and Associations: Overview of how groups and subgroups are structured

docs.title: Trainer Management: Create Training Packs and Review Sessions
docs.text:
Access Level

Trainer or Owner access is required. Trainer must also be enabled for the group.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Trainer Management lets you create reusable scenario packs, choose who can access them, and review user sessions. You can write packs yourself or ask AI to suggest drafts from recent development evidence.

How to access

Click Learning Management then Trainer.

The page contains two sections:

  • Training Packs for creating and maintaining packs
  • User Sessions for reviewing users' progress, answers, scores, and feedback

Captured 25 October 2026.

docs.title: Create a Training Pack Manually
docs.text:
1. Open Training Packs.
  2. Click New Pack.
  3. Enter a Pack name.
  4. Optionally enter a Description.
  5. Choose the evidence and audience settings.
  6. Click Add Scenario.
  7. Complete the scenario fields.
  8. Add further scenarios when required.
  9. Turn on Active when the pack is ready for users.
  10. Click Save and Close or Save and Continue Editing.
  11. Result: The pack is saved. Active packs are available to the selected audience.

Captured 25 October 2026.

docs.title: Pack Fields
docs.text:
Pack name, required

  • Use a clear name that users and trainers will recognise.

Active, optional

  • Only active packs can be started by users.
  • Leave this off while reviewing a new or AI-suggested pack.

Manual review, optional

  • Turn this on when a trainer must check and release coaching feedback before the user can see it.
  • The user is emailed when feedback is released.

Description, optional

  • Explain what the pack develops and when users should complete it.

Evidence scope, required

  • Select Whole group evidence to use relevant records from across the group when requesting AI suggestions.
  • Select Selected subgroup evidence to restrict suggestions to selected subgroups.

Target subgroups, optional

  • Leave this blank to make an active pack available across the group.
  • Select one or more subgroups to restrict who can see and start the pack.

docs.title: Scenario Fields
docs.text:
Title, required

  • Enter a short name for the scenario.

Internal scoring benchmark, required

  • Enter a value from 1 to 100.

Prompt, required

  • Describe the situation and what the user must respond to.

Rubric, required

  • Describe what a strong answer should demonstrate.

A pack must contain at least one complete scenario before it can be saved.

docs.title: Ask AI to Suggest a Pack
docs.text:
AI suggestions are drafts. Review every scenario, rubric, and scoring benchmark before activating the pack.

  1. In Training Packs, click Suggest a Pack.
  2. Optionally enter Focus areas.
  3. Select an Evidence period.
  4. Select at least one evidence source: Diaries, Assessments, or Development plans.
  5. Click Continue.
  6. Review the suggested pack in the Pack Editor.
  7. Edit the name, description, audience, scenarios, rubrics, and scoring benchmarks as needed.
  8. Turn on Active only when the pack is ready.
  9. Save the pack.

If you select Selected subgroup evidence, you must select at least one subgroup.

docs.title: Ask AI to Suggest a Scenario
docs.text:
1. Create or open a pack.
  2. Make sure the pack has a name, description, or other clear direction.
  3. Click Suggest a Scenario.
  4. Optionally enter Focus areas.
  5. Select the evidence period and at least one evidence source.
  6. Click Continue.
  7. Review and edit the suggested title, prompt, rubric, and scoring benchmark.
  8. Save the pack.

AI uses the selected development evidence only when a trainer requests a suggestion. It does not generate new scenarios when a user starts a session.

docs.title: Edit or Delete a Pack
docs.text:
• Select a pack to open it in the Pack Editor, make changes, then click Save and Close or Save and Continue Editing.
  • Turn off Active to stop new users from starting the pack.
  • Click the pack's delete action, then click Delete Pack to confirm permanent removal.

docs.title: Review User Sessions
docs.text:
1. Open the User Sessions tab.
  2. Find the session by user, pack, date, status, or summary.
  3. Open the session.
  4. Review each scenario's Prompt, Response, score, and Coaching Feedback.
  5. Click Print when you need a printable session record.
  6. Click Close to return to the session list.

Session statuses include In progress, Awaiting review, and Completed.

Captured 25 October 2026.

docs.title: Release Manually Reviewed Feedback
docs.text:
When Manual review is enabled for a pack:

  1. Open User Sessions and select a session marked Awaiting review.
  2. Open the scenario's Coaching Feedback tab.
  3. Review and, if required, edit Coaching feedback shown to the user.
  4. Optionally enter Internal review notes for trainers.
  5. Click Release feedback and notify user.
  6. Result: The feedback becomes visible to the user and the user is emailed.

docs.title: Delete a User Session
docs.text:
1. In User Sessions, click the session's delete action.
  2. Confirm the warning.
  3. Result: The session is permanently removed.

docs.title: Trainer is not enabled
docs.text: If the page shows Trainer is not enabled, the feature is not available for the group. A group owner can review the group's billing and AI feature settings.

docs.title: No evidence matched the selected controls
docs.text: Widen the evidence period, select another evidence source, choose a different subgroup, or add a scenario manually.

docs.title: AI is temporarily unavailable
docs.text: Keep your existing pack content and try the suggestion again later. You can always add a pack or scenario manually.

docs.title: The pack will not save
docs.text: Check that the pack has a name and at least one scenario. Every scenario requires a title, prompt, rubric, and scoring benchmark from 1 to 100.

docs.title: Printing does not open
docs.text: Allow pop-ups for MOS, reopen the session, and click Print again.

docs.title: Related Pages
docs.text:
• Trainer - Complete training packs as a user
  • AI Features - Configure AI feature access

docs.title: Admin: User Management
docs.text:
Access Level

Owner access required

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Manage all users in your organisation through the User Management page. View user lists, search for members, edit user details, create new accounts, change user names, reset passwords, manage group membership, upload profile pictures, and export user data.

docs.title: How to Access
docs.text: Click Admin then User Management

docs.title: Page Layout
docs.text:
When you open the page you see:

Search and Filter Section

  • Search box to find users by name or username
  • Group filter dropdown if you manage multiple groups
  • Search and All Users buttons

Export Section

  • Export button to download user list as CSV

User List Table

  • User profile pictures
  • Full names
  • Email addresses and phone numbers
  • Group memberships
  • Edit and action buttons

docs.title: Searching for Users
docs.text: Captured 25 October 2026. The member information shown is fictional.

docs.title: Search from the page header
docs.text:
Use the Search users... box at the top of a page to find a member without first opening User Management. Enter their name to show a result card. Select View Profile to view the member's profile, or Edit User in the administration row to open their record. Assessment buttons appear together on the Assessments row.

Captured 25 October 2026.

docs.title: Search by Name or Username
docs.text:
To find specific users:

  1. Enter a name or username in the Search User box
  2. Click Search
  3. Result: Only matching users appear in the table

docs.title: Filter by Group
docs.text:
If you manage multiple groups:

  1. Click the Filter by Group dropdown
  2. Select a group
  3. Result: Only users from the selected group appear

docs.title: View All Users
docs.text:
To return to the full list:

  1. Click All Users
  2. Result: The complete user list displays

docs.title: Editing User Details
docs.text:
To update a user's information:

  1. Click Edit next to the user's name in the list
  2. The page switches to edit view showing the user's current information

You can update these sections:

docs.title: Address Section
docs.text:
Captured 25 October 2026.

Search Address

  • Type an address in the search box
  • Select from the dropdown suggestions
  • Click Save Changes to apply the selected address

Current Address

  • Shows the currently saved address
  • Read only display

Phone Numbers

  • Phone Number - Primary contact number
  • Work Number - Work contact number
  • Secondary Number - Additional contact number

docs.title: Personal Details Section
docs.text:
Captured 25 October 2026.

Secondary Email Address

  • An additional email address saved on the member's profile.

Shirt Size

  • Optional profile detail. Enter the member's shirt size if it is useful to your organisation.

Pants Size

  • Optional profile detail. Enter the member's pants size if it is useful to your organisation.

Joined Your Group

  • The year the member joined your group.

docs.title: About Me Section
docs.text:
Rich text editor for user biography:

  • Use formatting toolbar for bold, italic and lists
  • Add links and formatted text
  • Displays on user profile page

When the AI features add-on is active and your role has AI Rewrite access, the editor shows a purple AI Rewrite button. Write a draft first, then select a passage to rewrite only that passage or leave it unselected to rewrite the whole biography. Review the result before saving the user's profile. See AI Features for access settings and troubleshooting.

docs.title: Profile Picture Section
docs.text:
Captured 25 October 2026.

Only appears if the user belongs to groups where you have administrator access:

Upload Picture

  1. Click Upload Picture

  2. In the Upload Profile Picture dialog, use Choose File or click Select Picture to open the file picker.

    Captured 25 October 2026.

  3. Select a JPG, PNG or GIF image that is no larger than 2 MB

  4. Adjust the square crop, then click Crop & Upload
  5. Result: The profile picture updates

Image Requirements

  • Formats: JPG, PNG, GIF
  • Maximum size: 2 MB
  • Automatically cropped to square

Remove Picture

  1. Click Remove Picture
  2. Confirm the deletion
  3. Result: Picture is deleted and replaced with default avatar

Alternative Method

You can also delete profile pictures from the Media page, which allows you to manage multiple profile images at once or delete orphaned profile pictures.

Multiple Groups

If the user belongs to multiple groups:

  • Select which group to upload the picture for using the dropdown
  • Pictures are stored separately for each group

docs.title: Saving Changes
docs.text:
After making updates:

  1. Click Save Changes at the top or bottom of the page
  2. Result: Confirmation message appears and changes are saved
  3. Click Back to return to the user list

docs.title: Changing a User's Name
docs.text:
The Change Name action appears in the member's header card when the account supports administrator name changes. It is not shown for every account.

To change a user's first name or surname:

  1. Click Edit user next to the person's name
  2. In the member header card at the top of the edit page, click Change Name
  3. Enter the required First Name and Last Name
  4. Click Update Name
  5. Result: MOS confirms the change and refreshes the member details

Name Validation

  • Names must contain only letters, spaces, hyphens and apostrophes
  • Both name fields are required

Username Changes

When you change a user's name, MOS updates their username using the new name. If that username is already in use, MOS adds a number to make it unique.

The user receives a confirmation email about the name change.

docs.title: Group Membership
docs.text:
To view and manage which groups a user belongs to:

  1. Click Edit user next to the user's name
  2. Scroll to the Group Membership section
  3. Review the groups, the licences remaining in each group, and the Member switch.

Captured 25 October 2026.

To add or remove the user from a group, turn its Member switch on or off. The change is saved immediately.

Tip

To change access levels or assign roles such as Viewer, Reviewer, Trainer, Communications, or Files Manager, use Membership and Roles.

docs.title: Add Single User
docs.text:
To create one new user:

  1. From Admin, select New user
  2. The Create a new user form appears
  3. Enter:
    • First Name (required)
    • Surname (required)
    • Email Address (required) - Valid email format
  4. Click Create User

What Happens Next

Result: MOS confirms the account details and opens the new member's record, where you can review group membership and add profile details. MOS sends a welcome email with sign-in details.

docs.title: Bulk Import Users
docs.text:
To add multiple users from a CSV file:

  1. From Admin, select Bulk import
  2. Click Download Example CSV to get the template
  3. Fill in the template with these columns:
    • FirstName
    • Surname
    • Email
  4. Select your completed file
  5. Click Upload & Preview
  6. Review each row and its status
  7. Fix any rows with errors and upload the corrected file again if needed
  8. Click Process [number] User(s) to continue with the valid rows
  9. Result: MOS shows the outcome for each row

Validation

Rows are checked for:

  • Required first name, surname and email address
  • Valid email format
  • Duplicate email addresses within the file

If an email address already belongs to an account, the preview marks the row as a warning and explains whether that account will be added to your group or restored.

Preview Table

The preview shows a table with these columns:

  • #: Row number from the CSV
  • First Name: User's first name
  • Surname: User's surname
  • Email: User's email address
  • Status: Badge showing Valid, Warning, or Error
  • Detail: Explanation of any issue found

Results

After processing, MOS shows the result for each row.

Warning

Check that you have enough available licences before importing.

docs.title: Resetting User Passwords
docs.text:
You can reset a user's password when they forget it or need a temporary password.

Availability: This action only appears for accounts that support password reset.

To reset a user's password:

  1. Find the member in the user list and click Reset password.
  2. Review the Confirm Password Reset message
  3. Click Reset Password to confirm
  4. Result: MOS confirms the reset and sends the user an email with temporary sign-in details

docs.title: Deleting Users
docs.text:
To remove a user from the system:

  1. Find the member in the user list and click Delete user
  2. Review the confirmation message
  3. Click Delete User to confirm
  4. Result: MOS removes the user and refreshes the list

Captured 25 October 2026.

Warning

If the person belongs to multiple groups, deleting them removes them from all groups. To remove them from only one group, use the Member switch in Group Membership.

Before Deleting

Consider if you should:

  • Remove them from specific groups instead of deleting entirely
  • Lower their access level instead
  • Keep the account but inform the user they no longer have access

docs.title: Exporting Users
docs.text:
Captured 25 October 2026.

To download your complete user list:

  1. Click Export in the Export Users section
  2. Result: CSV file downloads to your computer

CSV Contents

The export includes:

  • Username and name
  • Email and secondary email address
  • Last login date
  • Address and contact numbers
  • Groups the user belongs to

Uses

  • Audit records and compliance reporting
  • Import into other systems
  • Analysis and planning
  • Backup documentation
  • Licence verification

docs.title: Pagination
docs.text:
If you have many users:

  • 10 users display per page
  • Pagination controls appear at the bottom
  • Click page numbers to navigate
  • First, previous, next and last buttons available

docs.title: Multiple Group Management
docs.text:
If you administer multiple groups:

Group Filter

  • Filter dropdown appears in the search section
  • Select a group to view only its members
  • Select All Groups to view everyone

Multiple Groups Alert

If you belong to multiple groups with administrator access:

  • Alert banner appears at the top
  • Shows which groups you can manage
  • Helps you understand which users you can edit

docs.title: Validation Rules
docs.text:
First Name and Surname

  • Both fields are required when creating a user or changing a name
  • The Change Name form allows letters, spaces, hyphens and apostrophes

Email Address

  • Must be valid email format
  • Must contain @ symbol
  • Must have domain extension
  • Examples: user@example.com, name.surname@domain.co.au

Address

  • Search for a new address and choose a suggestion
  • The current address is read-only; save the form to apply the selected address

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
Best Practices

  • Update user details when their contact information changes
  • Export your user list when you need a current copy
  • Use bulk import for adding multiple users at once
  • Check licence availability before adding users
  • Use search to find users quickly in large lists
  • Remove users from groups they no longer need access to instead of deleting

When Changing Names

  • Inform the user before changing their name
  • Confirm spelling with the user
  • Tell them their username will change

Profile Pictures

  • Upload clear professional photos
  • Use consistent image quality across your organisation
  • Images are cropped to squares automatically
  • File size affects page load speed

docs.title: Cannot Edit User
docs.text:
Symptoms

  • Edit button is greyed out or missing
  • Error when clicking Edit

How to Fix

  1. Verify you have Owner access
  2. Check the user belongs to a group you administer
  3. Refresh the page
  4. Log out and log back in

Common Causes

  • Insufficient permissions
  • User belongs to a different group
  • Session expired

docs.title: Add an existing MOS user to your group
docs.text: Use the Member switch in the user's Group Membership section. See Group Membership.

docs.title: Bulk Import Errors
docs.text:
Symptoms

  • Some rows fail to import
  • Error messages appear in results

How to Fix

  1. Check CSV format matches the template exactly
  2. Verify all email addresses are valid
  3. Remove any duplicate emails
  4. Check that each row has a first name, surname and email address
  5. Save the file in CSV format
  6. Try uploading a smaller batch

Common Causes

  • Invalid email format
  • Duplicate emails
  • Wrong file format
  • Special characters in names
  • Missing required columns

docs.title: Profile Picture Not Uploading
docs.text:
Symptoms

  • Upload button does not work
  • Error message when uploading
  • Picture does not appear

How to Fix

  1. Check file size is under 2 MB
  2. Verify file format is JPG, PNG or GIF
  3. Try a different image file
  4. Check your internet connection
  5. Refresh the page and try again

Common Causes

  • File too large
  • Unsupported file format
  • Network connection issues
  • Browser cache problems

docs.title: Related Pages
docs.text:
• AI Features - Rewrite a member's About Me text
  • Change User Name - How users change their own names
  • Group Settings - Configure your group
  • Subgroup Membership - Manage subgroup access
  • Forgot Password - Password recovery process

docs.title: Auto-Appoint
docs.text:
Access Level

Appointer role or Owner access required

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Auto-Appoint uses your organisation's depth chart rankings to suggest the best available officials for an event. Rather than manually searching for officials, the system presents a ranked list based on score, tier, and availability — you review the suggestions and confirm with one click.

Auto-Appoint is not available in Passive Mode.

docs.title: How to Access
docs.text:
From the main menu under Owner Admin, click Appointments then Auto-Appoint.

You can also access it directly from an event detail panel: click the Auto-appoint link next to the event's grade.

docs.title: Before You Start
docs.text:
• The event must have a Depth Chart Grade assigned. You can set this when creating or editing the event.
  • Your depth chart must have officials ranked for that grade. See Depth Charting for setup.
  • For slot-based suggestions, set up Round Templates for the grade first.

docs.title: Selecting an Event
docs.text:
1. Choose an event from the Event dropdown. Events are listed with their date and title.
  2. Select the Season Year for the depth chart rankings you want to use.
  3. Click Load Suggestions.
  4. Result: The system shows ranked suggestions for the event.

Captured 25 October 2026.

If the selected event has no grade linked, an information message appears. Edit the event and assign a grade to proceed.

docs.title: Flat Suggestions (no template)
docs.text:
If no Round Template has been set up for the event's grade, a flat ranked list of officials appears.

The table shows each official with:

Column Description Rank Their position on the depth chart Official Name Tier Skill level badge (Elite, Senior, Developing, or Junior) Score Depth chart score Status Whether they are available, unavailable, or already assigned Role A dropdown to assign a role when appointing

Row colours:

  • Yellow row — Official has marked themselves unavailable on the event date
  • Green row — Official is already assigned to this event

Officials who are available are pre-selected. Officials who are already assigned have their checkbox disabled.

docs.title: Appointing from the Flat List
docs.text:
1. Review the suggested officials. Adjust checkboxes as needed.
  2. Select a Role for each official you intend to appoint (optional)
  3. Click Appoint Selected
  4. Result: The selected officials are assigned to the event. A success message confirms how many were appointed.

docs.title: Slot Suggestions (template exists)
docs.text:
If a Round Template has been set up for the event's grade, the system fills slots based on the template — one suggested official per slot.

The table shows each slot with:

Column Description Role The role this slot is for Slot Slot number within that role Suggested Official The highest-ranked available official for this slot Tier Skill level badge Score Depth chart score Swap A dropdown to choose a different official for this slot

docs.title: Swapping a Suggestion
docs.text:
If you prefer a different official for a slot:

  1. Click the Swap dropdown for that slot
  2. Select another official from the list (ranked by score, with unavailability noted)
  3. Select Skip slot to leave that position unfilled

docs.title: Appointing All Slots
docs.text:
1. Review the suggestions and swap any officials as needed
  2. Click Appoint All Slots
  3. Result: All filled slots are assigned to the event. A success message confirms the result.

docs.title: Round Templates
docs.text:
Round Templates define how many officials of each role are required for each grade. When a template exists for an event's grade, Auto-Appoint uses the slot-based view instead of the flat list.

Example: Premier Grade requires 2 Umpires and 1 Goal Umpire. Setting up a template for that grade means every Premier Grade event will show exactly those three slots when you use Auto-Appoint.

docs.title: Viewing Templates
docs.text: Scroll to the Round Templates section at the bottom of the page. Use the Grade filter dropdown and click Filter to view templates for a specific grade.

docs.title: Adding a Template Slot
docs.text:
1. Click Add Slot
  2. Select the Grade from the dropdown
  3. Select the Role from the dropdown
  4. Enter the Quantity (number of officials needed for this role, between 1 and 20)
  5. Click Save
  6. Result: The slot appears in the template table

Captured 25 October 2026.

Repeat for each role required for that grade.

docs.title: Deleting a Template Slot
docs.text: Click the Delete button on the row you want to remove.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Set up Round Templates for each grade before using Auto-Appoint. The slot-based view makes it much easier to see exactly what is needed.
  • Officials with a green Available status are the best candidates. Yellow Unavailable officials have indicated they are not free on that date.
  • You can use Auto-Appoint as a starting point and then manually adjust assignments on the Appointments page.

docs.title: "This event has no depth chart grade linked"
docs.text:
Edit the event and assign a Depth Chart Grade, then return to Auto-Appoint and load suggestions again:

  1. Go to Appointments
  2. Select the event
  3. Click Edit and assign a Depth Chart Grade
  4. Return to Auto-Appoint and load suggestions again

docs.title: No officials appear in suggestions
docs.text: No officials have been ranked on the depth chart for this grade and season year, or all officials are already assigned to this event. Check the Season Year dropdown — ensure it matches the year your depth chart was last updated, then go to Depth Charting and confirm officials are ranked for this grade.

docs.title: Suggestions show but the Appoint button is disabled
docs.text: No officials are selected in the flat list view, or all slots are set to "Skip slot" in the slot-based view.

docs.title: Related Pages
docs.text:
• Appointments — View and manage event staffing after appointing
  • Depth Charting Overview — Set up rankings used by Auto-Appoint
  • Availability — View official availability across the group

docs.title: Availability
docs.text:
Access Level

Appointer role or Owner access required to view group-wide availability. All users can record their own availability.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The Availability page gives administrators a full picture of which officials are available across any given month. It displays a colour-coded calendar matrix for the whole group, and a summary table showing availability percentages per official.

Officials can also record their own availability from their personal Appointments section.

docs.title: How to Access
docs.text: From the main menu under Owner Admin, click Appointments then Availability.

docs.title: Availability Matrix
docs.text:
The matrix shows every member of your group in rows, with dates across the top as columns.

Captured 25 October 2026.

Colours:

Colour Meaning Green Official has marked themselves available Red Official has marked themselves unavailable No colour No availability recorded for that date

docs.title: Navigating Months
docs.text: Use the ◀ and ▶ arrows on either side of the month heading to move between months.

docs.title: Summary Statistics
docs.text:
Three summary cards at the top of the page show:

  • Average availability % — the mean availability across all officials for the selected month
  • Officials ≥ 75% — how many officials are available for at least 75% of expected days
  • Expected days configured — the number of days per month used to calculate percentages

docs.title: Availability Analytics Table
docs.text:
Below the matrix, the analytics table lists every official with:

  • Available Days — number of days marked available in the selected month
  • Unavailable — number of days marked unavailable
  • Expected Days — the target number of days for the month
  • % Available — available days as a percentage of expected days

docs.title: Filtering by Subgroup
docs.text: Use the subgroup dropdown at the top to view availability for a specific subgroup rather than the whole organisation.

docs.title: Exporting Availability
docs.text:
1. Optionally select a subgroup from the dropdown
  2. Optionally tick Only include officials with at least one unavailable day to narrow the results
  3. Click Export CSV
  4. Result: A spreadsheet downloads showing official names, dates, and availability status

docs.title: Configuring Expected Days
docs.text:
Note: Only group owners can change this setting.

Expected Days tells MOS which days of the week officials are typically expected to be available. This is used to calculate the availability percentage shown in the analytics table.

Example: If your competition runs on Saturdays and Sundays, you would select Saturday and Sunday. A day in the month that is not a Saturday or Sunday does not count toward the total.

  1. Click Expected Days
  2. Tick the days of the week your officials are expected to be available
  3. Click Save
  4. Result: Availability percentages are recalculated using the updated day selection

Captured 25 October 2026.

docs.title: Passive Mode
docs.text: If your organisation is in Passive Mode, a notice appears explaining that availability is managed by an external system. Officials cannot record their own availability manually — it is imported from the external system.

docs.title: How Officials Record Availability
docs.text:
Officials manage their own availability from their personal accounts:

  1. The official navigates to Appointments → Availability
  2. They select a date on the calendar
  3. They mark themselves Available, Conditional, or Unavailable for that date
  4. For Conditional or Unavailable, they can add an optional condition or reason
  5. The record appears immediately in the admin matrix

Captured 25 October 2026. No availability is set for the displayed month.

docs.title: The matrix shows no data
docs.text: All cells in the matrix are blank. This occurs when officials have not recorded availability for the selected month, or your organisation is new and no availability data exists yet.

docs.title: Percentages look incorrect
docs.text: Availability percentages seem too high or too low. Click Expected Days and review which days are selected — ensure only the days your competition runs on are ticked, then save the changes. This is commonly caused by Expected Days not being configured, or officials recording availability on non-competition days.

docs.title: Related Pages
docs.text:
• Appointments — Assign officials to events (availability badges appear in the assign modal)
  • Auto-Appoint — Ranked suggestions show availability status

docs.title: Importing Appointments
docs.text:
Access Level

Owner access required

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The Import page lets you bring events, appointments, and availability records into MOS from a CSV or Excel file. This is the primary way to sync data when your organisation uses an external appointments system such as OfficialsHQ.

docs.title: How to Access
docs.text: From the main menu under Owner Admin, click Appointments then Appointments. Click Import in the top right corner.

docs.title: Before You Start
docs.text:
• You need a CSV or Excel (.xlsx) file exported from your external system, or prepared manually
  • For OfficialsHQ imports, export your allocations from OfficialsHQ first
  • Setting up Mappings before importing will save time and ensure officials are matched correctly

docs.title: Step 1: Choose Import Type
docs.text:
Select the type of data you are importing from the Import type dropdown:

Option What it imports OfficialsHQ Allocations Events and officials from an OfficialsHQ allocations export Events / Fixtures only Event details only, no official assignments Appointments (officials only) Appointments linked to existing events Availability Official unavailability records

The page shows the expected column names for the selected import type as a guide.

docs.title: Step 2: Select Your File
docs.text:
Click File (.csv or .xlsx) and choose your file, or drag and drop the file onto the dashed drop zone.

Accepted formats: .csv and .xlsx

Captured 25 October 2026.

docs.title: Step 3: Validate
docs.text:
Click Validate File. MOS reads the file and checks every row.

After validation, a results area appears showing:

  • Green badge — Number of rows that are ready to import
  • Yellow badge — Number of rows with warnings (they will still be imported)
  • Red badge — Number of rows with errors (they will be skipped)

A summary message explains what will happen when you commit.

docs.title: Validation Table (OfficialsHQ Allocations)
docs.text:
For OfficialsHQ and combined imports, a full preview table shows every row with:

  • Row number
  • Event date
  • Home team vs Away team
  • Official name
  • Role
  • Status badge:
    • Matched (green) — Official was found in MOS and will be assigned
    • Warning (yellow) — Official name was not matched; the appointment will be skipped
    • Event only (grey) — Row has no official (event will still be created)
    • Error (red) — Row has a critical problem and will be skipped entirely

Tip: If you see many Warning rows, go to the Mappings tab to set up name mappings, then re-validate.

docs.title: Unresolved Officials
docs.text:
If any official names in the file could not be automatically matched to a MOS user, they appear in the Unresolved Officials section with options to:

  • Map — Link the import name to a specific MOS user
  • Ignore — Mark the name to be silently skipped on all future imports

docs.title: Step 4: Commit
docs.text:
Once you are satisfied with the validation results, click Commit Import.

If you are importing appointments, an optional Replace Mode checkbox is available:

Replace mode — when ticked, any existing appointments that are not in your import file will be removed from the matched events. Use this when your import file represents the complete and final list of officials for those events.

Warning: Replace Mode removes appointments. Only use it when your file is the authoritative list.

After committing:

  • A success message confirms how many rows were processed
  • The import appears in the Import History table

docs.title: Import History
docs.text:
Below the upload area, the Import History table shows your recent imports with:

  • Date and time of the import
  • Import type
  • File name
  • Number of rows
  • Number of errors
  • Status badge (Committed or Failed)
  • A Download Error Report button (if there were errors)

docs.title: Mappings Tab
docs.text: Mappings let you define translations between names in your import file and records in MOS. Once saved, mappings are applied automatically on every future import.

docs.title: User Mappings
docs.text:
When an official's name in the import file does not exactly match their name in MOS, a User Mapping tells MOS who they are.

Example: The import file contains "J. Smith" but MOS has "John Smith" — a mapping links the two.

By default, the table shows only unresolved entries (names that have not been mapped yet). Toggle Show all to see every saved mapping.

docs.title: Adding or Editing a User Mapping
docs.text:
1. Click the Edit button next to a name
  2. Search for the MOS user in the search box and select them
  3. Alternatively, tick Ignore to permanently skip this name on future imports
  4. Click Save
  5. Result: The mapping is saved. Re-validate your import file to see the updated results.

Captured 25 October 2026.

docs.title: Removing a User Mapping
docs.text: Click the Delete button next to a mapping to remove it.

docs.title: Competition Mappings
docs.text:
When a competition or grade name in your import file does not match the grade name in MOS, a Competition Mapping tells MOS which grade it belongs to.

Example: The import file contains "Grade 1" but MOS has "1st Grade" — a mapping links the two.

By default, the table shows only unmapped entries. Toggle Show all to see all saved mappings.

docs.title: Adding a Competition Mapping
docs.text:
1. Click Add
  2. Enter the competition name exactly as it appears in your import file
  3. Select the matching MOS grade from the dropdown
  4. Click Save
  5. Result: The mapping is saved and existing events with that competition name will be linked to the selected grade automatically

Captured 25 October 2026.

docs.title: Editing a Competition Mapping
docs.text:
1. Click the Edit button next to a mapping
  2. Change the grade selection
  3. Click Save

docs.title: Tips for a Successful Import
docs.text:
• Validate before committing. Always check the validation results before clicking Commit Import.
  • Set up mappings first. Name mismatches are the most common cause of missed appointments. Use the Mappings tab to resolve them, then re-validate.
  • Use Replace Mode carefully. Only enable it when your file is the complete and final allocation for those events.
  • Check the Import History. If something goes wrong, download the error report to see which rows failed and why.

docs.title: Officials are showing as "Warning — not matched"
docs.text: Many rows show a yellow Warning badge with "not matched in MOS". This happens when the official's name in the import file is abbreviated or formatted differently to their MOS name, or the official is not a member of your group in MOS. Go to the Mappings tab, find the unresolved names in User Mappings, edit each one and map it to the correct MOS user, then return to the Import tab and click Validate File again.

docs.title: Events are created but appointments show 0 officials
docs.text: Import appears successful but events have no officials assigned. Check the validation preview table for rows showing Warning (not matched). Set up User Mappings for the unmatched names, then re-validate and commit again. This is caused by official names not being mapped before committing.

docs.title: Import shows "Failed" in history
docs.text: The import appears in history with a red Failed badge. Click Download Error Report next to the failed import, review the errors listed, fix the issues in your source file, and import again.

docs.title: Related Pages
docs.text:
• Appointments — Manage events and official assignments
  • Auto-Appoint — Automatically suggest officials using depth chart rankings

docs.title: My Appointments
docs.text:
Access Level

Available to all authenticated users. No special role required.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The My Appointments page shows all appointments assigned to you by your organisation's administrator. You can view upcoming fixtures, respond to appointment requests, and export your schedule to a calendar application.

docs.title: How to Access
docs.text: From the main menu, click Appointments then My Appointments.

docs.title: Before You Start
docs.text:
Your administrator must assign you to an event before anything appears here. If the page is empty, you have no upcoming appointments.

If your organisation manages appointments in an external system, MOS displays the schedule but does not show the Respond action. You can still use the diary actions on an appointment.

docs.title: Upcoming Appointments
docs.text:
The Upcoming tab shows appointments for events that have not yet occurred.

Each appointment shows:

  • Event title
  • Date and time
  • Home team vs Away team (if set)
  • Competition or grade
  • Venue name
  • Your assigned role
  • Your current response status (Pending, Accepted, or Declined)
  • Any notes added by the administrator

Captured 25 October 2026.

docs.title: Responding to an Appointment
docs.text:
When an administrator assigns you to an event, your appointment appears with a Pending status and a Respond button.

  1. Click Respond next to the appointment
  2. A prompt appears showing the event name
  3. Click Accept to confirm you are available, or Decline to advise you cannot attend
  4. Result: The status badge on your appointment updates immediately to Accepted or Declined

The names and fixture details shown are fictional.

Captured 25 October 2026. The fixture details shown are fictional.

Tip: Respond as early as possible so administrators can plan staffing.

docs.title: Appointment History
docs.text: The History tab shows appointments for events that have already occurred. Use this to review your past appointments, roles, and responses.

docs.title: Exporting Your Schedule
docs.text:
You can download your upcoming appointments as a calendar file to add to Google Calendar, Apple Calendar, Outlook, or any other calendar application.

  1. Click Export to Calendar (.ics) at the top of the page
  2. A file downloads to your device
  3. Open the file to import your appointments into your preferred calendar application
  4. Result: Your upcoming appointments appear as events in your calendar with the event title, date, time, venue, and role

Tip: Re-download the file whenever your appointments change to keep your calendar up to date.

docs.title: Linking an Appointment to a Diary Entry
docs.text:
If your organisation uses the Assessment Diary, you can link an appointment to a specific diary entry to track them together.

  1. Find the appointment you want to link
  2. Click Link Diary
  3. Choose your diary entry from the list, using the teams, date, venue and competition to identify the match
  4. Click Link
  5. Result: The appointment is linked. The button changes to Unlink

Captured 25 October 2026. The sample match details are fictional.

Captured 25 October 2026. The sample match details are fictional.

Only your diary entries in the current organisation are available to link. To remove a link, click Unlink on the appointment.

To start a diary entry for an appointment, click New Diary. The teams, date, venue and competition are prefilled from the appointment; complete the remaining fields and save the entry.

Captured 25 October 2026. The sample match details are fictional.

docs.title: Status Badges
docs.text: Badge Meaning Pending You have not responded yet Accepted You accepted the appointment Declined You declined the appointment Cancelled The event was cancelled by the administrator

docs.title: No appointments appear
docs.text: The page shows no upcoming appointments. Check the History tab — your appointments may be in the past. If nothing appears there either, contact your administrator to confirm you have been assigned to events. This happens when you have not been assigned to any upcoming events, or your organisation has not set up appointments yet.

docs.title: Respond button is not visible
docs.text: An appointment shows but there is no Respond button. This occurs when you have already responded, the event has been cancelled, or your organisation manages appointments in an external system.

docs.title: Related Pages
docs.text:
• Availability — Record which days you are available or unavailable
  • Home Dashboard — View a summary of your upcoming appointments
  • Assessments and Reviews — Create Diary entries, including one started from an appointment

docs.title: Appointments: Managing Events and Officials
docs.text:
Access Level

Appointer role or Owner access required

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The Appointments page is where administrators create events, assign officials, and track staffing across all fixtures. You can see every event for the season, check how many officials have been assigned, and manage individual appointments from a single page.

docs.title: How to Access
docs.text: From the main menu under Owner Admin, click Appointments then Appointments.

docs.title: Before You Start
docs.text:
Set up your Roles and Venues before creating events — these are needed when assigning officials and building events.

If your organisation uses an external appointments system, you may be in Passive Mode. In this mode, events and appointments are imported from that system rather than created manually. A blue notice at the top of the page will tell you if this is the case.

Captured 25 October 2026.

docs.title: Page Layout
docs.text:
The Appointments page has two panels:

  • Left panel — the event list with filters
  • Right panel — event details and assigned officials (appears when you select an event)

docs.title: Events List
docs.text:
The left panel shows all events for your organisation. Each event displays:

  • Event title
  • Date
  • Competition or round (if set)
  • Teams (if set)
  • Number of officials assigned, with a staffing badge showing how many are needed

Staffing badges:

Badge Meaning Green (e.g. 3/3) Fully staffed Yellow (e.g. 1/3) Partially staffed Red (e.g. 0/3) No officials assigned

Badges only appear when a Round Template has been set up for that event's grade.

docs.title: Filtering Events
docs.text:
Use the filters above the list to narrow down events:

  • From / To — date range filter
  • Grade — filter by depth chart grade

Click the filter controls to apply your selection.

Captured 25 October 2026.

docs.title: Pagination
docs.text: Use the Previous and Next buttons at the bottom of the list to move between pages.

docs.title: Creating a New Event
docs.text:
Note: Not available in Passive Mode.

  1. Click New Event
  2. Fill in the event details (see fields below)
  3. Click Save
  4. Result: The event appears in the list and is selected automatically

docs.title: Event Fields
docs.text:
Title, required

  • The name of the event, shown to officials when they are assigned
  • Example: Round 5 — Hawks vs Eagles

Date, required

  • The date the event takes place

Time

  • The start time of the event

Competition / Round

  • The competition name or round number, used for filtering and reporting

Venue

  • Select from your organisation's saved venues

Depth Chart Grade

  • Links the event to a grade from your depth chart, enabling the Auto-Appoint feature

Home Team / Away Team

  • The team names for the fixture

Notes

  • Any additional information for assigned officials

Respond By

  • A deadline date for officials to accept or decline their appointment

docs.title: Viewing and Editing an Event
docs.text:
Click any event in the left panel to see its details in the right panel.

Captured 25 October 2026. Names and sample fixture details are fictional.

The right panel shows:

  • Event title, date, time, venue, and teams
  • Respond by date (if set)
  • Grade (with an Auto-Appoint link if a grade is set)
  • Notes
  • Staffing summary (if a Round Template is configured for this grade)
  • All assigned officials with their status

To edit an event, click the Edit button (pencil icon) in the event header.

docs.title: Assigned Officials
docs.text:
The Assigned Officials section lists everyone appointed to the selected event.

Each entry shows:

  • Official's name
  • Appointment status badge
  • Role (if assigned)
  • Notes (if any)

Status badges:

Badge Meaning Pending Official has not responded Accepted Official has accepted Declined Official has declined Cancelled Appointment was cancelled

docs.title: Staffing Summary
docs.text: If a Round Template has been set up for the event's grade, a staffing table appears above the officials list showing how many officials of each role are needed and how many have been assigned.

docs.title: Assigning an Official
docs.text:
Note: Not available in Passive Mode.

  1. Select the event from the list
  2. Click Assign in the Assigned Officials header
  3. Start typing the official's name in the search box
  4. Select the official from the results
    • A green A badge means the official has marked themselves available on this date
    • A red U badge means the official has marked themselves unavailable
  5. Optionally select a Role from the dropdown
  6. Optionally enter Notes
  7. Click Assign
  8. Result: The official appears in the list with a Pending status

Tip: Availability badges help you avoid assigning officials who are already marked unavailable. You can still assign them if needed.

docs.title: Removing an Official
docs.text:
1. Find the official in the Assigned Officials list
  2. Click the Remove button (✕ icon) next to their name
  3. Confirm when prompted
  4. Result: The official is removed from the event

docs.title: Notify All
docs.text:
Send a reminder to every assigned official at once.

  1. Click Notify All in the event header
  2. Confirm when prompted
  3. Result: A notification is sent to all assigned officials for this event

docs.title: Re-notify One Official
docs.text:
1. Click the Re-notify button (bell icon) next to an individual official
  2. Result: A notification is sent to that official only

docs.title: Cancelling an Event
docs.text:
Note: Not available in Passive Mode.

  1. Select the event
  2. Click Cancel in the event header
  3. Confirm when prompted
  4. Result: The event is marked as cancelled. Assigned officials are notified. A Cancelled badge appears on the event.

docs.title: Deleting an Event
docs.text:
Note: Not available in Passive Mode.

  1. Select the event
  2. Click the Delete button (bin icon) in the event header
  3. Confirm when prompted
  4. Result: The event and all its appointments are permanently removed

Warning: Deleting an event cannot be undone.

docs.title: Exporting Events
docs.text: Click Export CSV to download the current event list as a spreadsheet.

docs.title: An official's availability badge is not showing
docs.text: No availability badge appears next to an official's name in search results. This occurs when the official has not recorded availability for that date, or when availability records exist but not for the exact event date.

docs.title: The staffing badge is not showing on an event
docs.text: Events show only an official count with no colour-coded badge. Check that the event has a Depth Chart Grade assigned, and that a Round Template has been set up for that grade.

docs.title: Related Pages
docs.text:
• Auto-Appoint — Use depth chart rankings to suggest and appoint officials automatically
  • Import — Import events and appointments from a CSV or Excel file
  • Availability — View official availability across the group
  • Roles and Venues — Configure the roles officials can be assigned to and manage venues

docs.title: Appointment Roles and Venues
docs.text:
Access Level

Owner access required to configure roles and venues

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Before you can make the most of the Appointments feature, you need to set up the roles officials can be assigned to, and the venues where events are held. Both are used throughout the appointments workflow — in event creation, official assignment, and auto-appoint suggestions.

docs.title: How to Access
docs.text:
• Roles: Owner Admin → Appointments → Roles
  • Venues: Owner Admin → Appointments → Venues

docs.title: Appointment Roles
docs.text:
Roles define what position an official fills at an event — for example, Umpire, Referee, or Goal Umpire. Roles appear as options whenever you assign an official to an event or configure a Round Template.

Captured 25 October 2026.

docs.title: Adding a Role
docs.text:
1. Click Add Role
  2. Enter a Role Name (required)
    • Example: Umpire, Goal Umpire, Referee
  3. Enter a Sort Order (optional)
    • Lower numbers appear higher in dropdowns throughout the system
    • Default is 0
  4. Click Save
  5. Result: The role appears in the roles table and is immediately available in event assignment and auto-appoint

Captured 25 October 2026.

docs.title: Editing a Role
docs.text:
1. Click the Edit button next to the role
  2. Update the name or sort order
  3. Click Save

docs.title: Deactivating a Role
docs.text: Click the Active toggle next to a role to deactivate it. Deactivated roles no longer appear in dropdowns when assigning officials. Existing appointments with that role are not affected.

docs.title: Deleting a Role
docs.text:
Click the Delete button next to the role and confirm when prompted.

Tip: If a role is no longer needed, deactivating it is safer than deleting it — deactivated roles are hidden from dropdowns but existing appointments remain intact.

docs.title: Appointment Venues
docs.text:
Venues are the locations where events take place. They can be linked to events when creating or editing them, and appear in official appointment notifications.

Captured 25 October 2026.

docs.title: Adding a Venue
docs.text:
1. Click Add Venue
  2. Fill in the venue details (see fields below)
  3. Click Save
  4. Result: The venue appears in the venues table and is immediately available in event creation

Captured 25 October 2026.

docs.title: Venue Fields
docs.text:
Venue Name (required) — the name of the venue as it should appear to officials. Example: Optus Stadium

Address — street number and name. Example: 333 Victory Parade

Suburb — Example: Burswood

State — Example: WA

Postcode — Example: 6100

docs.title: Editing a Venue
docs.text:
1. Click the Edit button next to the venue
  2. Update any of the venue details
  3. Click Save

docs.title: Deactivating a Venue
docs.text:
Click the Active toggle next to a venue to deactivate it. Deactivated venues no longer appear in the venue picker when creating or editing events. Existing events with that venue are not affected.

Note: Venues are deactivated, not deleted. This preserves the link to any existing events that use the venue.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Set up all your roles before creating events. Roles cannot be assigned to officials if they have not been created first.
  • Add all your regular venues at the start of the season so they are ready to select when creating fixtures.
  • Use the Sort Order on roles to control the order they appear in dropdowns — put your most common roles at the top with lower numbers.

docs.title: Related Pages
docs.text:
• Appointments — Create events and assign officials using the roles and venues you configure here
  • Auto-Appoint — Round Templates use roles to define staffing requirements per grade

docs.title: Exams
docs.text:
Access Level

All users can sit exams. Exam management requires Trainer or Owner role.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Complete exams that have been assigned to you. Answer questions, submit your responses, and view your results. Exams may be graded automatically or by your administrator.

How to Access: Click Assessments then Exams

docs.title: Finding Your Exams
docs.text:
Captured 25 October 2026.

  1. Open Assessments → Exams
  2. You see a list of exams assigned to you
  3. Exams show the title, due date, status, and actions available

Exam Status:

  • Available or Required: You can start the exam
  • Expired or Overdue: The exam's end date has passed, so you cannot start it
  • Passed or Failed: You have an attempt on record; open the exam to view your result

To include exams whose end date has passed, turn on Show expired exams above the list. The list reloads with expired exams included. When an exam is required, it appears as Overdue after its end date; other expired exams appear as Expired.

docs.title: How to Start and Complete an Exam
Starting the Exam
docs.text:
1. Find your exam in the list
  2. Click Start or Resume (if continuing from in progress)
  3. A modal window shows the exam name and instructions
  4. Click Start exam to begin

docs.title: During the Exam
docs.text:
The exam screen shows:

  • Question number buttons at the top - click any number to jump to that question
  • Previous and Next buttons - navigate between questions
  • Countdown timer - shows remaining time in minutes and seconds
  • Pass mark - the score needed to pass this exam
  • Question content - read carefully and select your answer

docs.title: Answering Questions
docs.text:
1. Read the question carefully
  2. Select your answer based on the question type:
    • Single choice: Click one correct option
    • Multiple choice: Check all correct answers
    • True/False: Select True or False
  3. Your answer is marked automatically as you select it

docs.title: Moving Through the Exam
docs.text:
You can navigate in several ways:

  • Click a question number at the top to jump directly to that question
  • Click Previous to go back to the previous question
  • Click Next to move to the next question
  • Use arrow keys on your keyboard: Left arrow = Previous, Right arrow = Next
  • The buttons disable when you reach the first or last question

docs.title: Submitting Your Exam
docs.text:
1. When you finish all questions, click Submit exam
  2. Your answers are submitted
  3. If the exam is auto-graded, you see your score immediately with a pass/fail result
  4. You may be offered the chance to See answers or Resit exam (if allowed)

Tips:

  • Take your time; questions may require careful reading
  • Watch the countdown timer to pace yourself
  • Use the question number buttons to review answers before submitting
  • Ensure a stable internet connection before starting
  • Avoid closing the browser or navigating away mid-exam

docs.title: Exam Results
docs.text:
After submitting your exam:

  • Your Score displays immediately if auto-graded
  • A Pass/Fail badge shows whether you achieved the pass mark
  • The score shows both your percentage and raw score (points earned vs. total available)
  • Some exams include explanations for correct answers
  • Your administrator may publish additional feedback or comments

docs.title: How to Review Past Results
docs.text:
1. Go to Assessments → Exams
  2. Look for Previous Results or Completed section
  3. Click an exam to view your score and details
  4. Review any feedback or explanations provided
  5. Questions are marked as correct or incorrect
  6. You can see all your answers side by side with the correct answers

docs.title: Retake an Exam (if allowed)
docs.text:
1. Go to Assessments → Exams
  2. Find the exam you want to retake
  3. If a Retake button appears, click it
  4. Complete the exam again following the steps above
  5. Submit your new responses

Note

Not all exams allow retakes. Check with your administrator if you're unsure.

docs.title: Check Pass Mark and Attempts
docs.text:
1. Open the exam details or look at the exam list
  2. Review Pass Mark and Maximum Attempts (if shown)
  3. If uncertain, contact your administrator

docs.title: Understand Your Score
docs.text:
After your exam is marked, you see:

  • Percentage Score: Your percentage of correct answers
  • Raw Score: Total points earned vs. total available
  • Pass/Fail: Whether you achieved the required pass mark (shown as a badge)
  • Individual question review: See which answers were correct and which were incorrect

docs.title: Exam will not start
docs.text:
Symptoms: The Start button is grayed out or doesn't work

How to Fix:

  1. Verify you have an assigned exam
  2. Check the exam availability window (it may not be open yet)
  3. Check your internet connection
  4. Log out and back in, then try again
  5. Try a different browser
  6. Contact your administrator if the issue persists

Common Causes:

  • Exam window not yet open
  • Exam window has closed
  • You don't have access to this exam
  • Browser/connection issue

docs.title: Answers not saving
docs.text:
Symptoms: Your responses disappear when you move to the next question

How to Fix:

  1. Wait for pages to load fully before clicking Next
  2. Avoid using the browser Back button
  3. Check your internet connection
  4. If the problem repeats, report it to your administrator immediately

Common Causes:

  • Network connectivity issue
  • Page didn't load completely
  • Using browser navigation while exam is loading

docs.title: Unexpected logout during exam
docs.text:
Symptoms: You're logged out and sent to the login page during the exam

How to Fix:

  1. Log back in with your credentials
  2. Return to Assessments → Exams
  3. Your progress may have been saved; click Resume to continue
  4. If progress didn't save, contact your administrator

Common Causes:

  • Session timeout due to inactivity
  • Network issue causing logout
  • System maintenance

docs.title: Can't submit the exam
docs.text:
Symptoms: Submit button is grayed out or doesn't work

How to Fix:

  1. Verify you have answered the questions you want to submit
  2. Click Submit exam button in the top right
  3. Check your internet connection
  4. Try again in a few moments
  5. Contact your administrator if submission fails repeatedly

Common Causes:

  • Network connectivity issue
  • Page didn't load completely
  • System timeout

docs.title: Time running out
docs.text:
Symptoms: The countdown timer shows you only have a few seconds left, or displays "Time is up!"

How to Fix:

  1. If time is running out, finish answering your remaining questions
  2. If time has run out, a modal appears automatically
  3. Click Submit exam in the modal to save your responses
  4. Any answered questions will be graded based on your answers
  5. Unanswered questions will count as incorrect

Tips:

  • Watch the countdown timer throughout the exam
  • Pace yourself to ensure you complete as many questions as possible
  • The timer shows both minutes and seconds remaining

docs.title: Related Pages
docs.text:
• Assessments and Reviews: Manage your other assessments
  • Reports: View your exam trends and pass rates

docs.title: Assessments and Reviews: Manage Your Development
docs.text:
Access Level

All users

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Create and manage your Diary and Plan entries, and view reviews and assessments assigned to you. Use bulk actions to keep things tidy and export your data when needed.

How to Access: Click Assessments

docs.title: My Assessments
docs.text:
A list of your match-related assessments and reviews.

  • Shows subject, date, association, status, and whether you have viewed it.
  • Use the pager to browse older items.

Captured 25 October 2026. Names and fixture details shown are fictional.

docs.title: Bulk actions
docs.text:
• Mark as read: Acknowledges reviewed items that you haven’t viewed yet.
  • Revert to confidential: Moves an item back to your private view (when allowed).
  • Delete: Removes your own entries that are not assigned assessments.

Result: A success banner confirms how many items were updated or skipped.

docs.title: My Plans
docs.text:
Personal planning entries (goals, actions, timeframes) with reviewer feedback when applicable.

  • Shows date, description, review state, and whether you have viewed it.

Captured 25 October 2026. Names and plan details shown are fictional.

docs.title: Bulk actions
docs.text:
• Mark as read: Acknowledges reviewed plans you haven’t viewed yet.
  • Archive: Moves plans to your archive to keep your main list focused.
  • Revert to confidential: Returns a plan to your private draft state (when allowed).
  • Delete: Removes selected plans.

Result: A success banner confirms how many items were updated or skipped.

docs.title: Create a Diary Entry
docs.text:
1. Click New Diary Entry.
  2. Select the appropriate template if prompted.
  3. Enter the match context and complete the sections provided.
  4. Save as a Draft or Submit as directed.

Captured 25 October 2026.

Result: The entry appears in your list. When reviewed, you can mark it as read.

docs.title: Start a Diary entry from an appointment
docs.text:
On My Appointments, click New Diary on the appointment you want to record. MOS opens a new Diary entry with the teams, venue, competition, and match date filled in. Complete the remaining fields and save or submit the entry as usual. See My Appointments for the appointment workflow.

Captured 25 October 2026.

docs.title: Using Autocomplete for Teams and Venues
docs.text:
When you enter Team A, Team B, or Venue information:

  • Start typing the team or venue name
  • After 3 characters, matching suggestions appear in a dropdown list
  • Click a suggestion to fill in the field automatically
  • This helps ensure consistent naming and reduces typing

Suggestions are drawn from teams and venues previously used in your group.

docs.title: Create a Plan
docs.text:
1. Click New plan entry.
  2. Add goals, actions, and any due dates.
  3. Save your plan; update over time as you progress.

Result: The plan appears in your list. When reviewed, you can mark it as read or archive it later.

docs.title: Dictate Diary and Review Text
docs.text:
When your group enables voice dictation and your browser supports it, a microphone button appears in diary and peer-review comment fields and the Your Feedback field on completed assessments.

  1. Place the cursor where the dictated text should appear.
  2. Click the microphone and allow access if prompted.
  3. Result: the microphone turns red and the text area is locked while MOS listens, keeping the insertion point in place.
  4. Speak normally. Australian English speech is added at the cursor as editable text after each completed phrase.
  5. Click the microphone again to stop listening and unlock the text area.
  6. Check and edit the transcript before saving or submitting it.

Dictation does not save or submit an entry by itself. If the button is missing, ask an Owner whether voice dictation is enabled in Group Settings and check the System Requirements.

docs.title: Use AI Rewrite in an Entry or Feedback Field
docs.text:
When your group has AI features enabled and your role has AI Rewrite access, a purple AI Rewrite button appears in rich-text fields used for diary entries, plans, peer reviews, and assessment feedback.

  1. Write your draft in the text field.
  2. Select a passage to rewrite only that passage, or leave the text unselected to rewrite everything in the field.
  3. Click AI Rewrite.
  4. Review and edit the replacement text.
  5. Save or submit the entry using the normal action.

The rewrite is a suggestion and is not saved automatically. Check that it still reflects your own observations and meaning. See AI Features for limits and troubleshooting.

docs.title: Create a Peer Review
docs.text: Peer reviews allow you to provide feedback on a colleague's performance (if your association enables this feature).

docs.title: Before You Start
docs.text:
• Peer reviews may not be enabled for all associations
  • Check if the New peer review button is visible on your My Assessments page
  • Contact your administrator if you're unsure whether peer reviews are available

docs.title: How to Create a Peer Review
docs.text:
1. On the Assessments page, look for the New peer review button
  2. If the button is greyed out or missing, peer reviews are not enabled for your association
  3. Click New peer review
  4. Select the colleague you want to review
  5. Complete the peer review template (specific fields depend on your association)
  6. Choose how to submit:
    • Draft: Save privately; you can edit later
    • Submit for Review: Send to administrators for publication; they can add comments before sharing with the colleague
  7. Click Save

Result: Your peer review is created and appears in your list.

docs.title: After Submission
docs.text:
• Draft peer reviews: Only you can see them
  • Submitted peer reviews: Administrators review and publish before the colleague sees them
  • Published peer reviews: The colleague receives an email notification and can view your feedback
  • Your colleague can then view your feedback in their My Assessments list marked as a peer review

docs.title: Viewing Peer Reviews You Received
docs.text:
When a colleague creates a peer review for you:

  1. You receive an email notification (if enabled)
  2. The peer review appears in your My Assessments list
